queries: TheAgentCompany Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks arXiv 2412.14161

sources_considered.why: The paper version available at the post date, with the 24% figure.
The v3 revision from September 2025 falls outside the target period. It is used as context under another claim.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv (Xu et al., Carnegie Mellon University)

receipt.public_excerpt: find that with the most competitive agent, 24% of the tasks can be completed autonomously. This paints a nuanced picture on task automation with LM agents -- in a setting simulating a real workplace, a good portion of simpler tasks could be solved autonomously, but more difficult long-horizon tasks are still beyond the reach of current systems.

evidence_items.explanation: The best agent completed only 24% of tasks, and harder long-horizon tasks were beyond all systems. This supports 'not close to ready for prime time'. The authors call the picture nuanced, because simpler tasks were often solved.

unresolved_gaps: The authors frame the result as 'nuanced', not as a flat failure. 'Prime time' is a judgment call.
